ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the graph of the inverse proportion function $y_{1}=\frac{k}{x}$ intersects with the graph of the linear function $y_{2}=x+b$ at point $A(1, 4)$ and point $B(-4, n)$. What is the value of $k$ and the area of $\triangle ABO$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} 
Given point $A(1,4)$ lies on the graph of the inverse proportion function $y_1=\frac{k}{x}$,\\
$\therefore k=1\times 4=4$,\\
$\therefore$ the expression for the inverse proportion function is $y_1=\frac{4}{x}$,\\
$\because$ point $B(-4,-1)$ also lies on the graph of the inverse proportion function $y_1=\frac{4}{x}$,\\
$\therefore n=4-4=-1$, that is, $B(-4,-1)$,\\
Substituting point $A(1,4)$ into the linear function $y_2=x+b$,\\
we get $1+b=4$, solving for $b$ gives $b=3$,\\
$\therefore$ the expression for the linear function is $y_2=x+3$;\\
Thus, the analytical expression for the inverse proportion function is $y_1=\frac{4}{x}$, and the linear function is found to be $y_2=x+3$;\\
Let the intersection of the line with the x-axis be C,\\
In $y_2=x+3$, when $y=0$, we get $x=-3$,\\
$\therefore$ the intersection of line $y_2=x+3$ and the x-axis is $C(-3,0)$,\\
$\because$ the segment $OC$ divides $\triangle AOB$ into $\triangle AOC$ and $\triangle BOC$,\\
$\therefore S_{\triangle AOB}=S_{\triangle AOC}+S_{\triangle BOC}=\frac{1}{2}\times 3\times 4+\frac{1}{2}\times 3\times 1=\boxed{7.5}$;

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, it is known that the graph of the inverse proportion function $y_{1}=\frac{k}{x}$ intersects with the graph of the linear function $y_{2}=x+b$ at point $A(1, 4)$ and point $B(-4, n)$. What is the value of $k$ and the area of $\triangle ABO$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} 
Given point $A(1,4)$ lies on the graph of the inverse proportion function $y_1=\frac{k}{x}$,\\
$\therefore k=1\times 4=4$,\\
$\therefore$ the expression for the inverse proportion function is $y_1=\frac{4}{x}$,\\
$\because$ point $B(-4,-1)$ also lies on the graph of the inverse proportion function $y_1=\frac{4}{x}$,\\
$\therefore n=4-4=-1$, that is, $B(-4,-1)$,\\
Substituting point $A(1,4)$ into the linear function $y_2=x+b$,\\
we get $1+b=4$, solving for $b$ gives $b=3$,\\
$\therefore$ the expression for the linear function is $y_2=x+3$;\\
Thus, the analytical expression for the inverse proportion function is $y_1=\frac{4}{x}$, and the linear function is found to be $y_2=x+3$;\\
Let the intersection of the line with the x-axis be C,\\
In $y_2=x+3$, when $y=0$, we get $x=-3$,\\
$\therefore$ the intersection of line $y_2=x+3$ and the x-axis is $C(-3,0)$,\\
$\because$ the segment $OC$ divides $\triangle AOB$ into $\triangle AOC$ and $\triangle BOC$,\\
$\therefore S_{\triangle AOB}=S_{\triangle AOC}+S_{\triangle BOC}=\frac{1}{2}\times 3\times 4+\frac{1}{2}\times 3\times 1=\boxed{7.5}$;

Image description: The attached figure is a plane rectangular coordinate system, with O marked at the origin, the x-axis horizontal to the right, and the y-axis vertical upward. In the figure there is an upward-slanting straight line passing through the point A(1,4) labeled in the first quadrant and the point B(-4,n) labeled near the third quadrant. There are also two branches of the hyperbola of an inverse proportional function, respectively in the first and third quadrants, and they intersect this straight line at the two points A and B.
Reasoning: According to the problem, A and B are both intersection points of the inverse proportional function y1=k/x and the linear function y2=x+b. First substitute A(1,4) into the linear function y2=x+b, obtaining 4=1+b, so b=3, and the linear function is y=x+3. Because the x-coordinate of B is -4, substituting into the straight line gives n=-4+3=-1, so B(-4,-1). Then substitute A(1,4) into the inverse proportional function y=k/x, obtaining 4=k/1, so k=4. Now the vertices of the triangle are A(1,4), B(-4,-1), and O(0,0). Use the coordinate determinant area formula: S=1/2|x_A y_B-x_B y_A|=1/2|1×(-1)-(-4)×4|=1/2|-1+16|=15/2=7.5.
